page: Amazon Web Services r5d.xlarge is a memory-optimized Nitro-based virtual server designed for workloads needing a high memory-to-vCPU allocation paired with high-speed local NVMe storage. Powered by a 3.1 GHz Intel Xeon 8259CL processor, the instance provides 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It includes 32.0 GB of DDR4 RAM running at 3 GHz, equating to 8.0 GB per vCPU. The instance also features a bundled 150 GB local NVMe SSD instance store volume and a 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. No hardware graphics accelerators are present.

Benchmark results place the computational throughput of the r5d.xlarge in lower percentiles compared to modern fleet averages. CPU workloads evaluated via stress-ng registered 1282.98 for single-core and 3364.35 for multi-core, while Geekbench recorded scores of 1048.0 single-core and 2271.0 multi-core. PassMark tests produced a overall CPU score of 4268.48 and a database operations score of 1422.21, reflecting bottom-quartile compute capability. Memory performance remains functional, with PassMark memory scoring 2137.13 in the average tier, supported by uncached large-block read bandwidth of 26.76 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 22.97 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the r5d.xlarge is positioned around high resource density in memory and physical storage rather than raw computational throughput. The integrated NVMe SSD provides fast, low-latency temporary storage without incurring network-attached volume overheads, making it suitable for caching layers, Redis deployments, temporary database scratch spaces, and light in-memory operational workloads that do not demand extensive compute cycles.

It operates with a 1 Gbps baseline network speed and has no GPU accelerators. The 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio yields an average PassMark memory score of 2137.13 alongside memory read throughput of 26.76 GB/sec for large blocks. Computational benchmarks reflect lower-quartile performance, including a Geekbench multi-core score of 2271.0 and a multi-threaded stress-ng score of 3364.35. The server is well aligned with memory-intensive workloads that require low-latency scratch disk access, such as caching nodes, in-memory datastores, and mid-tier transactional databases.
